key_insight: MedMO shows that a multimodal LLM trained end-to-end on large-scale, domain-specific medical data with a staged alignment and grounding recipe can substantially improve modality alignment and grounded clinical reasoning for medical images.
problem_solved: Bridges gaps that prevent MLLMs from clinical use—limited domain coverage, poor alignment between diverse medical image encoders and language backbones, and weak grounded reasoning/explanations for image-based clinical queries.
method: Curate and train exclusively on large-scale, domain-specific medical data spanning diverse imaging modalities and paired clinical text.

Multi-stage training: (i) cross-modal pretraining to align heterogeneous visual encoders with a medical language backbone, (ii) modality-aware fine-tuning to preserve diagnostic features, and (iii) grounding/instruction tuning to produce clinically grounded explanations and reasoning.
Design evaluation and prompting strategies to measure grounding, interpretability, and modality-specific performance in clinical scenarios.
impact: Enables more reliable, interpretable multimodal models for medical imaging tasks, lowering barriers to clinical adoption and accelerating development of downstream diagnostic and decision-support applications.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram showing multiple visual encoders fused into a single medical language backbone

Before/after examples: input medical image + model diagnosis/explanation to highlight grounded reasoning
Evaluation dashboard mockup comparing grounding and modality-alignment metrics versus baseline MLLMs
paper_title: MedMO: Grounding and Understanding Multimodal Large Language Model for Medical Images
paper_authors: Ankan Deria, Komal Kumar, Adinath Madhavrao Dukre, Eran Segal, Salman Khan
